title: Inside the sandbox
brief: A hosted agent's compute follows the session, not the request. Idle timeout, sandbox size and where state lives are dials you set before launch, and each one moves cost, latency or data loss.

blocks.md:
In a hosted agent, compute follows the *session*, not the request [[r2]]. A session is **Active** while it serves traffic, goes **Idle** after the idle timeout and is **Resumed** by the next request. `$HOME` and `/files` are persisted on idle and restored on resume. The idle timeout is set per agent version from 2 to 60 minutes, default 15. A session is deleted permanently after 30 days of inactivity.

Scale is per session, with no replica count and no warm pool. Billing follows the CPU and memory consumed across active sessions, so oversizing multiplies cost by concurrency. The concept page gives no numeric rates and links to the Foundry Agent Service pricing page, so model cost from that page, not from this guide.

blocks.title: Hosted session lifecycle
blocks.alt: A session starts Active, becomes Idle after the idle timeout, is Resumed by a new request and returns to Active. After 30 days idle it is deleted.

blocks.title: Active allocation that drives the bill

vars.v: sessions that are Active at the same time, not Idle
0.5 vCPU with 1 GiB, 1 vCPU with 2 GiB, or 2 vCPU with 4 GiB
up to 20 GiB at 1 vCPU or larger, about 20 percent reserved, shared with the image and `$HOME`

blocks.example: 200 active sessions at 2 vCPU and 4 GiB hold **400 vCPU and 800 GiB**. The same load at 1 vCPU and 2 GiB holds 200 vCPU and 400 GiB. The docs advise the next size up only when sustained peaks pass about 70 percent of allocation.

items.symptom: Uploaded files vanish after about five weeks
items.cause: The session was inactive for 30 days and was deleted, taking `$HOME` with it
items.fix: Write durable artifacts to storage you own. Alert on sessions that approach 30 idle days (inference).

items.symptom: Users see each other's saved preferences
items.cause: The key-value state store was not partitioned per end user
items.fix: Partition by end user id and test with two users in one agent.

items.symptom: The first message after a quiet period is slow
items.cause: The session moved to Idle and state had to be restored on resume (inference)
items.fix: Measure resume latency. A longer idle timeout trades resume latency against more active-session time.

items.cause: Support for the initial-preview hosted agent backend ended and routing moved to a dedicated endpoint per agent
items.fix: Redeploy on the session-sandbox model and replace the old adapter packages with `azure-ai-agentserver-responses` or `azure-ai-agentserver-invocations` [[r11]].

items.title: Go deeper: versions are immutable snapshots

blocks.md: Each create-version call snapshots the image, resources, environment variables and protocol configuration [[r2]]. An endpoint serves one version and sends 100 percent of traffic to it. Traffic splitting is not supported, so a canary needs a second agent name or a client-side router (inference).

items.title: Go deeper: long-running work is preview

blocks.md: The 2026-08 Foundry articles on resilience for long-running hosted agents, crash recovery, steering an in-flight turn, stream with reconnect and a human-in-the-loop approval step were all marked preview on 2026-10-13 [[r10]]. **Background mode** keeps work going after the request returns. **Resilient execution** keeps work going after the hosting process stops. They solve different problems, so name which failure you are covering.

items.title: Go deeper: the model deployment is a separate dial

blocks.md: The agent's model has its own deployment type [[r22]]. `GlobalStandard` is the docs' starting point and may process in any region. `DataZoneStandard` stays inside the US, EU or APAC zone. `Standard` stays inside one geography. `GlobalBatch` gives a 50 percent discount with a 24 hour target. Hosted agents were listed in 31 regions on 2026-10-13, and the list is stated to grow.

quiz.q: A fleet holds 120 active sessions at the 1 vCPU and 2 GiB size. How many GiB of memory are allocated across the active sessions?
quiz.explain: 120 sessions x 2 GiB = 240 GiB. Billing follows CPU and memory consumed across active sessions, so moving to the 2 vCPU and 4 GiB size would double this to 480 GiB at the same concurrency. Idle sessions do not count as active.

quiz.q: Support reports that a user's uploaded working files are gone. The user last opened the agent five weeks earlier. Which cause fits?

code.code:
session s-81f2 last active: 35 days ago
status: not found

options: The 2 to 60 minute idle timeout expired and `$HOME` was wiped on idle
The endpoint served a newer version and discarded files from the older one
The files were stored in `/files`, which is deleted on every resume
A session is deleted after 30 days of inactivity and takes its state with it
quiz.explain: Idle persists `$HOME` and `/files` and resume restores them, so the idle timeout is not the cause. Versions are immutable snapshots of image, resources and config, not a store that wipes files. `/files` uploads land in `$HOME` and are restored on resume. The 30 day inactivity limit matches 35 days.

quiz.q: Put the life of one hosted session in order.
items: Requests arrive and the session is Active
No traffic for the idle timeout, so the session is Idle and state is persisted
A new request arrives and the session is Resumed with state restored
No activity for 30 days and the session is permanently deleted
quiz.explain: State is persisted when the session goes Idle and restored when it resumes. Permanent deletion is the last step and only follows 30 days of inactivity.

takeaways: Compute follows the session: Active, Idle, Resumed, then deleted after 30 days inactive
Cost is active sessions times allocation, so right-size only after peaks pass about 70 percent
An endpoint serves one immutable version, so traffic splitting needs another design
Durable data belongs in a store you own, with per-user partitioning
